name: Y-front fly
summary: A cut for a brief in which two panels overlap in a Y shape at the front, so that the garment opens without a button and holds the body.
how: Cut the front in two pieces with a curved seam in the shape of a Y.
Lap one piece over the other and stitch the two together at the base.
Set an elastic band into the waist.

origin.note: Arthur Kneibler designs a short brief with an overlapping Y-shaped fly.

adoptions.via: Coopers, Inc. launched the Y-front brief in a store in Chicago on 19 January 1935.
